title: LightAVSeg: Lightweight Audio-Visual Segmentation
claim: Our lightweight models sit in the fast, accurate corner of the efficiency-accuracy plot, beating heavier baselines on both axes.
layout: 1 bubble scatter plot, latency vs accuracy, with Faster and Stronger arrows
description: A single bubble scatter plot. The x-axis is latency in ms, from 0 to 1300. The y-axis is MS3 mIoU in percent, from 25 to 60. Bubble size appears to grow with model size. Each bubble is labeled with a gray leader line. Red bubbles are the authors' models: Ours-SeaFormer-T, -B, -L and Ours-ResNet50. They sit toward the upper left, with SeaFormer-L bold and outlined in black. Baselines use other colors. SelM is green, AVSBench is blue and AVSegFormer is purple. The baselines are mostly larger, slower and less accurate. Red arrows at the top and right read Faster, pointing left, and Stronger, pointing up. A light dashed grid sits behind the bubbles. The eye goes first to the bold red Ours-SeaFormer-L bubble in the upper left.
caption: Efficiency-Accuracy Trade-off. We evaluate all models on the MS3 benchmark, and inference speeds are measured on a Snapdragon 8 Elite mobile CPU. Our method LightAVSeg outperforms heavy SOTA methods in both speed and accuracy on mobile device.
abstract: Audio-Visual Segmentation (AVS) targets pixel level localization of sounding emitting objects in videos. However, existing models rely on dense cross-modal attention with quadratic computational cost, limiting their suitability for resource efficient deployment. Most efficiency oriented methods focus on backbone reduction and overlook the interaction module as the primary bottleneck. This paper proposes LightAVSeg, a lightweight framework that replaces heavy attention with a decoupled design for semantic filtering and spatial grounding, resulting in interaction costs that scale linearly with spatial resolution. Furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary alignment loss to enforce semantic consistency during training with zero inference overhead. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LightAVSeg achieves a new state-of-the-art among lightweight methods: with 20.5M parameters ~1/7 of AVSegFormer), it reaches 50.4 mIoU on the MS3 benchmark and enables efficient inference on a mobile processor.
